The test was hard, so, I still passed.
The test was hard, but I still passed.
The test was hard I still passed.

choices.text: The data were incomplete, therefore, the study was repeated.
The data were incomplete therefore the study was repeated.
The data were incomplete; therefore, the study was repeated.
The data were incomplete; therefore the study was repeated, and incomplete.

choices.text: Studying at night is better than studying in the morning.
Regular practice is what makes revision work.

In the first and last sentences

choices.text: Answer from what usually happens in a lesson.

Return to that sentence and answer fifteen minutes.

Pick the only answer with a number in it
Find the sentence that mentions cost and read it again
Choose the answer that sounds most reasonable

choices.text: She never makes the same mistake twice.
She treats her mistakes as useful.

The lights caused the fall in crime
The town has no other safety measures

Students borrow more when they have more free time

The library will keep the longer hours next year

choices.text: Many students say weekends feel more relaxed.
Students who revised for 20 minutes daily scored 12% higher after a term.
Revision is an important part of any course.
Teachers often recommend a quiet place to study.

choices.text: Two teachers recorded fewer errors in their classes
A study measured clearer vowels after eight weeks

The writer enjoys reading aloud at home

choices.text: Students who wrote by hand recalled 20% more a week later in a controlled trial
Handwriting has been used for centuries

practice.question: A writer claims that handwriting notes helps memory more than typing them. Which is the strongest evidence?

choices.text: To prove the rule is wrong.
To make the rule easier to understand.

practice.question: A paragraph explains a rule, then adds a worked example. Why is the example there?

choices.text: To focus the reader on the problem the paragraph answers
To show that the writer is unsure

explanation: A purpose question asks what the writer is doing, not what the words mean.
practice.question: Why might a writer begin a paragraph with a question?

choices.text: To give an example of the rule
To restate the rule more simply
To limit the rule just stated

explanation: It marks an exception, which narrows the rule rather than supporting it.
practice.question: A paragraph explains a rule, then adds: “This is not true of irregular verbs.”  Why is that sentence there?

explanation: 'may' and 'thin evidence' hold back from a firm claim, so the tone is cautious.

practice.question: “The proposal is, frankly, a waste of everyone’s time.”  What is the tone?

choices.text: It gives an example of the idea before it.

choices.text: It qualifies the claim made before it
It gives an example of the claim

choices.text: It repeats the first half in other words
It gives an example of the first method
It weighs a drawback against an advantage

explanation: 'though costly' admits a drawback before giving the stronger advantage.
practice.question: A sentence reads: “The first method is cheap; the second, though costly, is far more accurate.”  What does the second half do?

explanation: The small sample is the reason for the caution, so the link shows a result.
practice.question: Choose the best transition.  “The trial used only ten subjects; ___, its findings should be treated with care.”

choices.text: The reason she finished early was because the paper was short.
She finished early due to the fact that the paper was short.
She finished early because the paper was short.
She finished early owing to the fact of the shortness of the paper.

explanation: Say it once, in the fewest clear words.
practice.question: Choose the most concise version.

choices.text: What we should do is begin now.
We should begin at this point in time.
It is now that we should begin to start.

explanation: Say it in the fewest clear words.
practice.question: Choose the most concise version.

choices.text: The committee came to the decision that the proposal should be rejected.
The proposal was rejected by the committee at that time.
It was the committee that made the decision to reject the proposal.

explanation: Say who did what in as few words as the meaning allows.
practice.question: Choose the most concise version.

choices.text: Please say that again for me.
Please repeat that again for me.

practice.question: Which phrase is redundant?

practice.question: Which word best completes the sentence?  “Check that your figures are ___ before you hand the work in.”

explanation: 'brief' means short.

explanation: In this sentence “rapid” means very fast.

practice.question: Which word best completes the sentence?  “The ___ growth of the city surprised the planners.”

explanation: 'decline' means to go down.

explanation: In this sentence “benefit” means an advantage.

explanation: 'benefit' means an advantage.

explanation: 'impact' means an effect.

explanation: 'obtain' means to get.

practice.question: Read the sentence: “The task requires full concentration.”  As it is used here, “require” most nearly means…

explanation: 'require' means to need.

explanation: In this sentence “demonstrate” means shows clearly.
